# Design and dependencies

Why Hyprland is built the way it is, what it needs from other ACO components, which libraries it uses and which versions it was tested with.

## Why it is built this way

- Responsive instead of pretty: no animations, blur, shadows or gaps – maximum screen space.
- Several monitors are the normal case: focus and window jumps, window slots (`Super + F1…F4`), workspace swap, a monitor tool with profiles; new monitors arrange themselves to the right.
- The configuration is **Lua**; `scripts/gen-docs.py` generates the key list straight from it so documentation and bindings cannot drift apart.
- It pulls the other desktop packages (terminal, menu, bar, wallpaper, tmux, Yazi, Dolphin, settings app); the ACO media apps and the browser are optional groups in as dependencies so an installation works immediately.

## What this configuration needs from others

| Component | Why |
| --- | --- |
| [Kitty](https://aco-kitty.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) | Default terminal (`Super + Enter`), also for `kitty -e yazi` and `kitty -e tmux` |
| [rofi](https://github.com/Akademie-Olympia/aco-rofi) | Launcher and all menu scripts through `aco-menu` (`settings.sh`, `powermenu.sh`, `windowswitcher.sh`, `askpass.sh`) |
| [Waybar](https://aco-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/waybar/) | Started with the session (`Super + Shift + B` reloads it) |
| [Wallpaper](https://aco-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/wallpaper/) | Backgrounds at start and on `monitor.added`; `Super + Shift + W` |
| [tmux](https://aco-tmux.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) | `Super + Shift + Enter` opens Kitty with the tmux session `main` |
| [Yazi](https://aco-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/yazi/) | `Super + Y` opens Yazi in a terminal |
| Dolphin (themed through aco-qt) | `Super + E` opens the graphical file manager |

## Who needs this configuration

| Component | Why |
| --- | --- |
| [Waybar](https://aco-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/waybar/) | Workspaces through the Hyprland IPC; the power menu calls `powermenu.sh`, `hyprlock` and `hyprctl` |
| [Wallpaper](https://aco-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/wallpaper/) | `hyprctl` and `swaybg`; the session calls `wallpaper apply` at start and on plug-in |
| [Zsh](https://aco-zsh.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) | `SUDO_ASKPASS` points to `askpass.sh` (graphical password prompt) |

## Notes

- `brightnessctl`, `wl-clipboard`, `grim`, `slurp` and `satty` are only used by the scripts (`screenshot.sh`) and shortcuts – without them exactly the matching key is missing.
- `Super + Shift + D` opens `monitors.sh`, which manages monitors and writes `monitors.local.lua` – that file lives outside the package.
- Notifications from the scripts use Hyprland's built-in `hyprctl notify`; no notification daemon is required.

## Shared foundations

These rules apply to **every** ACO component:

- **One repository per component**, with its own `PKGBUILD` and CI. Each configuration can be installed, tested and developed on its own;
  after a push the central registry builds the signed package ([packaging overview](https://aco-arch-dotfiles.readthedocs.io/en/latest/arch-package/)).
- **Pacman is the only updater.** No git pull at runtime; `aco` only merges new defaults with your changes (`.pacnew`).
- **Your copy, not the package's.** `~/.config/<module>` points to `~/.local/share/arch-dotfiles/config/<module>/`; the package stays untouched in `/usr/share/arch-dotfiles/<module>/`.
- **One theme:** colours, fonts and rounding come from `aco-theme` templates in every component, so light/dark, accent and transparency switch everywhere at once.
- **The core** `aco-arch-dotfiles-core` (the `aco` command, activation, backups, synchronisation) is a dependency of every package.
